findings.title: Fresh installs skip GitHub-user verification
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, when Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises Integration.DoesNotExist the code immediately returns pipeline.next_step() with no comparison of pipeline.fetch_state('github_authenticated_user') to the installer. That is the normal first-install path (proven by test_basic_flow which creates an Integration with no prior webhook). An attacker can complete installation without ever matching the GitHub App installer, or win a race against the installation webhook that creates the Integration row, defeating the security check this PR claims to add.

findings.title: Unsafe sender lookup can 500 instead of failing install
findings.body: The check uses integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] directly. Metadata sender is optional (build_integration only sets it if state.get("sender"), and installation API fixtures have no sender). If an Integration exists without sender metadata, this raises KeyError and returns HTTP 500 instead of the intended github-integration-failed.html error page, breaking reinstalls and leaking internal error handling.

findings.title: Token exchange and user lookup have no error handling
findings.body: OAuthLoginView.dispatch calls safe_urlopen for the code->token exchange and get_user_info for /user outside any try/except (only safe_urlread/parse_qsl is wrapped). Network errors, non-2xx from GitHub, timeouts, or ApiError from get_user_info will propagate as an unhandled exception and HTTP 500. The PR description says bad/reused code should show the installation-failed page, but only the missing-access_token case is handled; all transport/API failures crash instead of returning error(request, ...).
